To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in normal infants and children the terminal negative deflections of the P waves in Leads V 1 and V 2 are usually small and that with increasing degrees of left atrial volume load, these negative deflections increase in amplitude and duration, and that the product of these two measurements, the terminal P -V 1 index, is an excellent indicator of the presence or absence of left atria enlargement in the pediatric age group.
an abnormal terminal P wave in Lead 1 is a reliable electrocardiographic indicator of left atrial volume overloading in children.

abnormal negativity of the terminal P-V _{1} deflection is the most sensitive and specific indicator of left atrial volume over-load in children, and correlates quite well with the size of the left atrium as measured by roentgenography.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an electrocardiographic method for identifying left atrial enlargement.
the evaluation of a new electrocardiographic method for the identification of left atrial abnormalities.
the development of electrocardiographic methods of recognizing left atrial enlargement, and with the evaluation of these methods as indicators of left atrial size in children.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
abnormality of the terminal P-V1 index in the electrocardiogram of children is the most sensitive indicator of left atrial volume overloading.

the P-V 3 index is the most sensitive electrocardiographic indicator of left atrial volume enlargement, that it is abnormal in 92 percent of children with left ventricular volume overload, and that it correlates quite well with increased left atrial volume as determined by the roentgenographic method.
the terminal P-V _{1} index, when greater than 0·02 mm. sec. in a child with a normal P-R interval, is a reliable indicator of left atrial hypertrophy or dilatation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the terminal P-V1 index is a reliable electrocardiographic sign of left atrial volume load, but not of pressure load.
the terminal P-V1 index is an accurate electrocardiographic index for the recognition of left atria enlargement, and is superior to other measures of left atria abnormality.

the electrocardiogram, particularly the scalar electrocardio- gram, is a useful method for the recognition of left atrium enlargement in children, and that the most reliable electrocardiographic sign of such enlargement is an abnormally negative P-V 2 deflection, as indicated by the terminal P-V index.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the P wave in the V1 lead can be used to diagnose left atrial enlargement.

the terminal P-V1 index, a simple electrocardiographic measurement, can identify left atrial enlargement and may be useful as a guide to the need for surgical intervention in children with ventricular septal defects or mitral regugitation.
